newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas up, naphtha dips on arb.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas up, naphtha dips on arb.

text.p: Aggressive buyers bid up gasoline prices on Thursday amid tight supplies while naphtha fell on talk on arbitrage arrivals, traders said.
Naphtha March swaps fell to $23.55/$23.75 per barrel from $23.80/$24.00 on Wednesday as sentiment started to falter.

Some traders said the recent firmness in the naphtha market might ease in April and May as a major and a Swiss trader were heard bringing two Mediterranean cargoes, with an additional six following, to the Far East.

Some Japanese refiners were also heard locking margins into the current firm market by selling naphtha-Dubai cracks at around $5-$6 per barrel for the third quarter. One trader said the crack is normally around $3.

Kuwait is likely to conclude term contracts with Asian buyers for around 2.4 million tonnes of full-range naphtha lifting March 1997-February 1996 on Friday at a record premium of around $13.50 per tonne over Mideast quotes, sources said.
Singapore's light distillate stocks, comprising gasoline, reformate and naphtha, fell 897,000 barrels to 5.019 million barrels, TDB figures showed for the week ending February 26.
Traders said the tightness in gasoline extended up to March, with still no sellers emerging to meet buyers on the Singapore fob market.
Unleaded 95-octane lifting March 22-26 was bid up to $27.80 per barrel, up 40 cents from Wednesday.
Two buyers for the 92-octane grade raised bids to $27.60 for a March 17-21 cargo and $26.90 for a later March 22-24 cargo, up $1.00 on the day.
Sentiment continued to build on Taiwan's issue of its first half April reformate import tender on Wednesday, just after it had awarded its second half March tenders last week, traders said.

Industry sources in India told Reuters the country's gasoline requirements for March were already covered by the one tender awarded earlier this month. It had bought around 90,000 tonnes of leaded 87-octane which it bought at $1.30 per barrel over Singapore 92-octane spot quotes.

A Japanese trader was awarded Petroleum Authority of Thailand's (PTT) tender to sell 90,000 barrels of natural gas liquids (NGL) lifting in March at 50 cents over Singapore naphtha quotes on a cost-and-freight basis to Singapore.
The tender, to sell the three 30,000-barrel cargoes from Sri Racha, which closed February 24, was sold for gasoline blending in Singapore, sources said.

PTT sources told Reuters excess supplies has prompted NGL export tenders since February due to the start-up in January of a new gas separation plant No.3 at Sri Racha, which processes natural gas into liquid petroleum gas (LPG), NGL, methane and
ethane.
Industry sources also said domestic refiner Thai Oil Co Ltd had reduced the volume of NGL it takes from Sri Racha because it is using an alternative blending component for gasoline.
PTT sources could not say whether it would issue a tender for April, saying that it would depend on Thai Oil's requirements.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
